## Why This Is Asked
This question probes practical, scalable secrets management for CI/CD in a multi-cloud, multi-tenant setup, focusing on reducing leakage risk.

## Key Concepts
- GitHub Actions OIDC
- Secrets management with per-environment vaults
- Short-lived credentials and rotation
- Secret scanning and policy-as-code (OPA)
- IR runbooks and containment steps

## Code Example
```yaml
permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - name: Configure AWS credentials
        uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@v1
        with:
          role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/GitHubActionsRole
          aws-region: us-east-1
```

- How would you measure reduction in secrets leakage and MTTR?
- How would you adapt this for a multi-cloud or hybrid environment?

## Why This Question Is Asked

## Code Example
```rego
package policy.tenant_isolation

default allow = false

allow {
    input.tenant == data.tenants[input.tenant_id].owner
    input.action == "read"
    input.resource_namespace == input.tenant_id
    not exceeds_quota(input.tenant_id, input.request_size)
}

allow {
    input.tenant == data.tenants[input.tenant_id].owner
    input.action == "write"
    input.resource_namespace == input.tenant_id
    input.token_expires_at > time.now_ns()
}

exceeds_quota(tenant_id, size) {
    data.tenants[tenant_id].quota_used + size > data.tenants[tenant_id].quota_limit
}
```

- What monitoring alerts would trigger automatic containment actions?
